criterion_scores.expected_or_correct: Preserve CuAAC transformation, Cu/C catalyst, acetone solvent, 150 C, liquid phase.
criterion_scores.rationale: The design correctly translates the batch CuAAC reaction to a continuous flow packed-bed process using the specified Cu/C catalyst and acetone solvent. The transformation, modality, and phase regime are preserved.

criterion_scores.expected_or_correct: Benzyl azide, phenylacetylene, acetone, Cu/C catalyst present.
criterion_scores.rationale: All required reagents (benzyl azide, phenylacetylene), solvent (acetone), and catalyst (Cu/C in cartridge) are present and correctly assigned. No unsafe materials introduced.
Concentrations (0.25 M azide, 0.275 M alkyne) and equivalents (1.1) match the batch protocol exactly. Feed composition is coherent.

Temperature (150 C) and pressure (20 bar) are correctly mapped. The design correctly identifies that 20 bar maintains acetone in the liquid phase at 150 C. Stage boundaries are appropriate for a single-stage flow process.

The topology (Pump -> Reactor -> BPR -> Collector) is executable and correctly ordered. All necessary unit operations (pumping, heating, pressurizing, collecting) are present. No mixer is needed for a single feed.

criterion_scores.expected_or_correct: Molar flows consistent with concentration and flow rate.
criterion_scores.rationale: Liquid material balance is correct. 0.1 mL/min * 0.25 M = 25 umol/min azide. 0.1 mL/min * 0.275 M = 27.5 umol/min alkyne. Ratio 1:1.1. Total flow 0.1 mL/min.

criterion_scores.expected_or_correct: Residence time calculation consistent with volume and flow.
criterion_scores.rationale: The design correctly calculates nominal residence time (3 min) based on geometric volume (0.3 mL) and flow (0.1 mL/min). It also correctly identifies the distinction between geometric volume and liquid holdup, estimating true contact time (1-1.5 min). This is a physically plausible and numerically closed calculation.
Gas process is false. No gas reagents used.
Multistage process is false. Single reactor stage.

All equipment IDs (pump_xcube_hplc, reactor_cuc_cart_030, heater_xcube, bpr_xcube_20, collector_amber_100, safety_cuaac_shield) are from the authoritative inventory. Operating conditions (150 C, 20 bar, 0.1 mL/min) are within equipment limits.
Pressure (20 bar) is sufficient to keep acetone liquid at 150 C. Flow rate is low, minimizing pressure drop. Product solubility is addressed. Transport assumptions are plausible.

Benzyl azide is an energetic azide. The design mandates the use of the blast shield (`safety_cuaac_shield`) and secondary containment. Pressure relief is provided by the vented collector and BPR. Hazards are recognized and controlled.
The procedure includes feed prep, assembly, leak test, priming, steady-state collection, shutdown, flush, and work-up. It is reproducible.

The design explicitly states assumptions (catalyst loading, void fraction) and unresolved questions. It does not guarantee yield but proposes a screening experiment. Evidence and uncertainty are calibrated honestly.

cross_criterion_notes: The design correctly handles the transition from batch slurry to flow packed-bed by retaining the catalyst in the cartridge.
The distinction between geometric residence time and liquid holdup residence time is correctly identified and explained, preventing a potential error in interpreting conversion data.
Safety controls for the azide are robust and use the specific inventory item provided.
